---
title: "Run it, inspect it, change it"
---
## First run

From the repository root, with Conda and Quarto installed:

~~~bash
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate lidar-forest-structure
lidar-forest download
lidar-forest run
lidar-forest validate
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
quarto preview
~~~

The download is approximately 74 MB. The full source is scanned in chunks; only the buffered window enters PDAL. Results go to ignored data/processed/.                                                                   

The report includes committed figures and a run manifest so it renders without executing the point-cloud workflow. Running the workflow refreshes report/assets/: inspect changes before committing.

## A second run

Existing output directories are never overwritten. Choose a new one:

~~~bash
lidar-forest run --output work/second-run
lidar-forest validate work/second-run
~~~

Compare scientific values and QC summaries rather than binary equality across GDAL/PDAL versions. Hashes verify one run's files. The tested environment inventory documents this local run.

## Notebook

[Download the walkthrough](../notebooks/01_walkthrough.ipynb). It validates locally processed results, displays figures, inspects coordinates and interprets label disagreements. Source has no saved outputs. Run from the repository root or notebook directory.                                             

## A different area

Copy config/example.yml and adjust bounds within the tile. Preserve a buffer covering the interpolation radius and SMRF window. Bounds must be divisible by resolution. Inspect source classes and units.

For a new source, obtain authoritative horizontal/vertical metadata and review its license and classification scheme. Unreviewed datum changes are rejected. Output metadata currently expects NAVD88 and a different datum requires implementation and verification.

## Files worth reviewing

- lidarforest/core.py: coordinate checks, indexing and interpolation.
- lidarforest/workflow.py: ingestion, PDAL comparison, staged outputs.
- data/source.json: pinned download, attribution and reuse limitation.
- config/example.yml: processing parameters.
- data/processed/run.json: local audit.
- data/processed/normalized_subset.laz: original classes plus extra dimensions.
- tests/test_core.py: numerical, coordinate and PDAL tests.

GitHub CI processes and validates the actual example, executes the notebook and renders a report artifact.
